topic: First-time home buyers: FHSA ($8,000/yr, $40,000 lifetime), HBP ($60,000, 15-year repayment, deferral for first withdrawals 2026–2028), both usable for the same home; home buyers' amount up to $10,000

example.note: example (not a CRA rule): two people who each qualify as first-time home buyers and meet every FHSA/HBP condition for the same qualifying home; maximums shown; FHSA room only from the year the account is opened ($8,000/yr, carry-forward up to $8,000); HBP needs enough RRSP savings; home buyers' amount (line 31270) is a non-refundable credit on up to $10,000, shared between spouses.

sources.fhsa: canada.ca FHSA: annual limit $8,000, lifetime $40,000, unused room carried forward up to $8,000 (CRA tax tips 2025, via search 2026-11-12)
sources.hbp: canada.ca What is the Home Buyers' Plan: up to $60,000 per participation period; repay within 15 years; for first withdrawals Jan 1 2026–Dec 31 2028 the repayment start is deferred to the fifth year after the first withdrawal
sources.both: canada.ca HBP: you can use the HBP and a qualifying FHSA withdrawal for the same qualifying home if all conditions are met
sources.hbta: CRA line 31270 home buyers' amount: up to $10,000, can be split with a spouse (taxtips.ca, CRA line 31270 page)
